key_insight: An optimal perturbation reveals the dynamical route from a splitting seed through an edge state to the successful division of a turbulent pipe-flow puff.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how turbulent puffs proliferate could inform prediction and control of laminar–turbulent transition in pipe systems.
method: Apply nonlinear nonmodal analysis to a reduced-order model to optimize a puff-splitting seed.
Use the optimized evolution to define a splitting-progress coordinate in phase space.
Dynamically align chaotic realizations for ensemble averaging of splitting dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports recovery of the full Navier–Stokes splitting dynamics, a strong velocity inflection in the optimal seed, and power-law scaling of its energy threshold with Reynolds number.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify the tested Reynolds-number range or quantitative validation errors, limiting assessment of generalizability.
paper_title: An Optimal Seed Reveals the Dynamical Route to Spontaneous Splitting of Turbulent Puffs
